title: 2021 Fall AMC 12B Problem 21
statement: For real numbers \(x,\) let \[ \begin{aligned} P(x) &= 1 + \cos(x) + i\sin(x) \\ &\quad {}- \cos(2x) - i\sin(2x) \\ &\quad {}+ \cos(3x) + i\sin(3x) \end{aligned} \] where \(i = \sqrt{-1}.\) For how many values of \(x\) with \(0 \le x \lt 2\pi\) does \[P(x) = 0?\]

solutions.text:
Group by Euler’s formula: \(P(x) = 1 + e^{ix} - e^{2ix} + e^{3ix}.\) The imaginary part is \[ \begin{gathered} \sin x - \sin 2x + \sin 3x \\ = (\sin x + \sin 3x) - \sin 2x \\ = \sin 2x(2\cos x - 1). \end{gathered} \]

This vanishes when \(\sin 2x = 0\) (so \(x = 0, \tfrac{\pi}{2}, \pi, \tfrac{3\pi}{2}\)) or \(\cos x = \tfrac12\) (so \(x = \tfrac{\pi}{3}, \tfrac{5\pi}{3}\)).

Checking the real part \(1 + \cos x - \cos 2x + \cos 3x\) at each of these values gives \(\pm 2\) or \(1,\) never \(0.\) So no \(x\) makes \(P(x) = 0.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Write \(P(x) = 1 + e^{ix} - e^{2ix} + e^{3ix}\) and require both the real and imaginary parts to vanish
The imaginary part factors as \(\sin(2x)(2\cos x - 1)\)
